newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGAL AND FRANCE BOTH HUNGRY FOR GOALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGAL AND FRANCE BOTH HUNGRY FOR GOALS.

text.p: With Portugal and France both out to remedy a severe lack of goals, the emphasis is sure to be on attack in Wednesday's soccer friendly in the northern city of Braga.
As preparations for the 1998 World Cup finals in France gather pace, both sides have something to prove to critics who say they have too often lacked punch in front of goal.

Despite going 30 matches without defeat until a 1-0 away loss to Denmark last October, coach Aime Jacquet's French side has been under fire for uninspired performances and a lack of efficiency up front.
The Portuguese have been inconsistent in their campaign to reach the finals for which France automatically qualify as hosts.
They had the better of a 0-0 draw against qualifying group nine favourites Germany before Christmas but typically failed to turn their advantage into goals.

"At this stage, there are no such things as friendlies," said coach Artur Jorge who knows French soccer well having led Paris Saint-Germain to the league title in 1994. "We are going to go flat out against a very strong opponent."
Jorge has added striker Domingos Oliveira, just returned after a four-month lay-off for injury, to the squad that played Germany in December.
But Oliveira, who was top scorer in the Portuguese league last season, was likely to start on the bench as he has yet to play a full game for Porto.

Jacquet was equally determined to make the most of one of his few remaining chances to hone the squad before this year's Tournament of France, something of a World Cup dress rehearsal in which Brazil, Italy and England -- all past world champions -- will take part.
The main changes should be in midfield, where Jacquet is expected to field Sampdoria's Pierre Laigle and maybe try the young Ibrahim Ba who is having a brilliant season with Bordeaux.
Up front, AC Milan's Christophe Dugarry, back in the squad for the first time since being injured in the Euro 96 quarterfinals, could be paired with Metz's Robert Pires.
